title: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge
body:
Read the chapter → [Joshua 20](/bible/joshua/20)

**[Joshua 20:1-3](/bible/joshua/20#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/joshua/20#v1)</sup> The Lord also spake unto Joshua, saying,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/joshua/20#v2)</sup> Speak to the children of Israel, saying, Appoint out for you cities of refuge, whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses:
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/joshua/20#v3)</sup> That the slayer that killeth any person unawares and unwittingly may flee thither: and they shall be your refuge from the avenger of blood.

- Now that every tribe had its inheritance, cities of refuge had to be instituted, as the Lord spake by the hand of Moses: that the slayer that killeth any person unawares and unwittingly may flee thither, and they shall be your refuge from the avenger of blood.
- Unwittingly means unknowingly; remember the word wittingly in [Genesis 48](/bible/genesis/48), where Israel guided his hands knowing what he was doing. This is accidental death, not intentional murder, like leaving a co-worker shut in the freezer by mistake because you were focused on going home.
- Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 19:1-3](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v1)</sup> When the Lord thy God hath cut off the nations, whose land the Lord thy God giveth thee, and thou succeedest them, and dwellest in their cities, and in their houses;
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v2)</sup> Thou shalt separate three cities for thee in the midst of thy land, which the Lord thy God giveth thee to possess it.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v3)</sup> Thou shalt prepare thee a way, and divide the coasts of thy land, which the Lord thy God giveth thee to inherit, into three parts, that every slayer may flee thither.

    Moses gave the instruction to separate cities of refuge in the midst of the land; in Joshua 20 Joshua is applying the law.
  - **[Deuteronomy 19:4-6](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v4)</sup> And this is the case of the slayer, which shall flee thither, that he may live: Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past;
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v5)</sup> As when a man goeth into the wood with his neighbour to hew wood, and his hand fetcheth a stroke with the axe to cut down the tree, and the head slippeth from the helve, and lighteth upon his neighbour, that he die; he shall flee unto one of those cities, and live:
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v6)</sup> Lest the avenger of the blood pursue the slayer, while his heart is hot, and overtake him, because the way is long, and slay him; whereas he was not worthy of death, inasmuch as he hated him not in time past.

    The case of the slayer: two neighbours go into the wood to hew wood, the axe head slips from the helve and lights upon his neighbour that he die; he hated him not in time past, so he was not worthy of death.
  - **[Numbers 35:11-12](/bible/numbers/35#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/numbers/35#v11)</sup> Then ye shall appoint you cities to be cities of refuge for you; that the slayer may flee thither, which killeth any person at unawares.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/numbers/35#v12)</sup> And they shall be unto you cities for refuge from the avenger; that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment.

    The cities of refuge were appointed that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment.
  - **[Exodus 21:12-13](/bible/exodus/21#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/exodus/21#v12)</sup> He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death.
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/exodus/21#v13)</sup> And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.

    The law goes back to Exodus: he that smiteth a man that he die shall surely be put to death, but if a man lie not in wait and God deliver him into his hand, a place is appointed whither he shall flee.

- The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.

  Precepts:
  - **[Nehemiah 13:21](/bible/nehemiah/13#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/nehemiah/13#v21)</sup> Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the sabbath.

    Nehemiah said, if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you; the same spirit and speech is in our people to this day.
  - **[Deuteronomy 19:11-13](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v11)</sup> But if any man hate his neighbour, and lie in wait for him, and rise up against him, and smite him mortally that he die, and fleeth into one of these cities:
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v12)</sup> Then the elders of his city shall send and fetch him thence, and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die.
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v13)</sup> Thine eye shall not pity him, but thou shalt put away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, that it may go well with thee.

    But if any man hate his neighbour and lie in wait and smite him mortally, the elders of his city shall fetch him from the refuge and deliver him to the avenger of blood; thine eye shall not pity him.
  - **[Deuteronomy 19:21](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/deuteronomy/19#v21)</sup> And thine eye shall not pity; but life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

    Life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: that was the judgment instituted in that time; today we are under different laws of the land, and you forgive your brother seventy times seven.
  - **[Numbers 35:22-25](/bible/numbers/35#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/numbers/35#v22)</sup> But if he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or have cast upon him any thing without laying of wait,
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/numbers/35#v23)</sup> Or with any stone, wherewith a man may die, seeing him not, and cast it upon him, that he die, and was not his enemy, neither sought his harm:
    >
    > <sup>[24](/bible/numbers/35#v24)</sup> Then the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments:
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/numbers/35#v25)</sup> And the congregation shall deliver the slayer out of the hand of the revenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, whither he was fled: and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.

    If he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or cast a stone seeing him not, the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood and deliver the innocent slayer back to his city of refuge.

- The murderer cannot run to a city of refuge to lay low; those cities were not established for him. Even today a killer can cross the border into another jurisdiction and go free, and that is evil; but when Israel controlled the land you could not cross a border to get away with murder, for the elders would deliver you right back to the city you came from. Your sin will find you out.

**[Joshua 20:6](/bible/joshua/20#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/joshua/20#v6)</sup> And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, and until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days: then shall the slayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.

- The slayer shall dwell in that city until he stand before the congregation for judgment: the congregation had to see whether it was a mistake or intentional, questioning him on what he was doing and why, just like a courtroom.
- He also dwelt there until the death of the high priest of those days; then the slayer shall return to his own city and his own house, the city from whence he fled.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 35:25](/bible/numbers/35#v25)**
    > <sup>[25](/bible/numbers/35#v25)</sup> And the congregation shall deliver the slayer out of the hand of the revenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, whither he was fled: and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.

    The congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.
  - **[Numbers 35:26-28](/bible/numbers/35#v26)**
    > <sup>[26](/bible/numbers/35#v26)</sup> But if the slayer shall at any time come without the border of the city of his refuge, whither he was fled;
    >
    > <sup>[27](/bible/numbers/35#v27)</sup> And the revenger of blood find him without the borders of the city of his refuge, and the revenger of blood kill the slayer; he shall not be guilty of blood:
    >
    > <sup>[28](/bible/numbers/35#v28)</sup> Because he should have remained in the city of his refuge until the death of the high priest: but after the death of the high priest the slayer shall return into the land of his possession.

    If the slayer comes outside the border of his city of refuge before the death of the high priest and the revenger of blood finds him and kills him, the revenger shall not be guilty of blood; the refuge is protective custody, and he was to remain in it.

**[Joshua 20:7-9](/bible/joshua/20#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/joshua/20#v7)</sup> And they appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, and Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath–arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/joshua/20#v8)</sup> And on the other side Jordan by Jericho eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness upon the plain out of the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/joshua/20#v9)</sup> These were the cities appointed for all the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation.

- They appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah; and on the other side Jordan by Jericho they assigned Bezer out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.
- These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation: until he gets a fair trial.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 17:6](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v6)</sup> At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; but at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.

    At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.
  - **[Matthew 18:15-17](/bible/matthew/18#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/matthew/18#v15)</sup> Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/matthew/18#v16)</sup> But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/matthew/18#v17)</sup> And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.

    If thy brother trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault alone; if he will not hear, take one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established, and then tell it unto the church.

- If your brother trespasses against you, you do not go and shoot, stab, or fight him; you speak to him alone, and if he hears you, you have gained your brother. This law of righteous judgment is what is missing in the cursed cities of our people, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, who have not learned to apply the scripture and await righteous trial.
- Not everything is a Matthew 18: [Matthew 18](/bible/matthew/18) goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend, because many times what you heard is just a tale.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 19:13-17](/bible/sirach/19#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/sirach/19#v13)</sup> Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/sirach/19#v14)</sup> Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again.
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/sirach/19#v15)</sup> Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/sirach/19#v16)</sup> There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart; and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/sirach/19#v17)</sup> Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the most High.

    Admonish a friend, for many times it is a slander; believe not every tale, and do not threaten a Matthew 18 over what only needs a correction.
  - **[Luke 17:1](/bible/luke/17#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/luke/17#v1)</sup> Then said he unto the disciples, It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him, through whom they come!

    Offences will come, it is inevitable; we build stronger bonds with brothers and sisters through adversity, so endeavor to keep the unity.
  - **[1 John 3:15](/bible/1-john/3#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/1-john/3#v15)</sup> Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.

    The spirit of anger and hatred transitions to murder; whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer.

- When you are angry you are not thinking logically; precepts are not coming to your mind, only carnal solutions. Do not go and talk to a brother while you are upset, and do not cleave to another backbiter or gossiper to feed your anger; cleave to somebody positive that is a peacemaker and solution minded.
- Give place to the law of the Most High: whatever situation you are going through, the solution is in the Bible, so do not let anger close the book on you. Sometimes the answer is to suffer wrongfully, and what matters is not who is right but what the right thing to do is according to the Bible.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Peter 2:19](/bible/1-peter/2#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/1-peter/2#v19)</sup> For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.

    This is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully; but examine yourself before you use this precept to play the victim, for the Lord knows what is behind closed doors.
